summary:
Fixer E (M3 fix round 2) has finished E1–E5 in the working tree. Nothing is committed and no value moved: only comments and docs changed, so nothing was re-blessed. 14 files changed, all listed below. M2's code is untouched, `docs.rar` is untouched, and the goldens are unchanged.

**The final `lune run scripts/verify` exits 1, the machine 28–74 % busy (median 40 %).** Tools, sourcemaps, T-META-07 and both luau-lsp passes are clean, then 735 pass and 1 fails: T-PERF-01, on F2's longest stretch (0.489 ms against 0.35). Every functional case passes. A 30-minute wait for a quiet machine (17:57–18:27) found none. My own scratch dumps of the plausible set ran during 18:00–18:09 of that wait, so the machine was not idle for its whole length.

**E1: a face flush on a thin part.** Text only, in §4.4, Sampling's header (its claim is now qualified), §5's promise, §0.5, §5.6, §17.2 and O10. Cover's header claims nothing on this and is unchanged. V1's figures hold on this tree:
- C09's core cut along its diagonal: Sharpening 0.1904 Normal → 0.2225 Hard.
- F5 with a 0.05-thick blade: 0.1440 → 0.2224 Hard.
- F5: 0.0989 → 0.1563.
- C02 and C13: 0.1318 → 0.1832.
- F5's exposed blade area: 1.1440 → 0.5720 + 0.6826.

In ordinary builds the band is HIDE_OFFSET/b of the contact (b is the Wedge's thickness across it), on the higher-ranked part's face. On the §5.5 fixtures it is 5.86 % of C09's exposed area, 0.33 % of C13's, and 0.05–0.20 % of the other Wedge fixtures'.

O10 now costs both ways out:
- **(i) as built:** the band only adds exposed area in the measure; in the verdict it can keep a part.
- **(ii) a segment probe**, tried as a scratch variant of the measure only:
  - no §5.5 tier moves; C09 drops 0.3201 → 0.2432 (Hammering) and 0.1904 → 0.0955 (Sharpening);
  - the diagonal cut then plays as the whole blade;
  - on the plausible set: d moves on 5,191 designs and the tier on 197, all Hard → Normal; 185 of them are built on C09;
  - cost: × 1.04–1.27 on the worst valid designs, so the slowest would go from 54.8 ms to about 65 ms quiet;
  - the verdict's half is described, not built.

**E2.**
- E-S2.13: the bit-identity sentence is rescoped, and a new bullet records what fix round 1 moved beyond the 70 fixtures, re-measured against fixer D's changes.
- §4.1 now lists the build's departures from the prototype, re-measured.
- §16.18 and Edge's comment say SAMPLE_X/SAMPLE_Y move values, re-measured.
- T-PERF-01's order: nothing needs it last, so the text now says where it runs instead.
- One-line notes: on the three T-DIF-04 pins and the 11 cases fixer B moved to t.slow.

**E3.**
- A Wedge written its other way: only C09's bevel moves, ΔG 0.0007, through M2's surface samples (O11 and others).
- The X-mirror move is traced and re-measured (E-S2.13 and fixer C's open issue in M3-notes).

**E4.** The ordinary-load timings are in §14.1, §14.11, §17.2 and E-S2.13. README no longer claims verify is green.

**E5.** All 88 decision marks carry their number. Every stated exception is named at §5's promise with its O-number; this added a round part's sampled overlap under a shift (O11). O7–O11 each state what the build does and what each option costs.

specEdits: §0.5 Factors row: two new limits. Under O11, the samples of round parts (their writing, and a shift's rounding where they overlap) and of a Wedge's surface (its writing). Under O10, a face flush on a part thinner than HIDE_OFFSET (a blade cut along its diagonal, a bevel's thin edge).

§4.1: the build departs from the prototype in §4.6 and §5.2 since fix round 1. On the prototype's 66 fixtures Thinness differs by up to 0.237 (P3), EdgeLength by up to 0.083 (P2), and 15 step values of 14 fixtures differ; before fix round 1 only P1's did. Reference.spec pins M2; Factors.spec and Edge.spec (OFF_PROTOTYPE) pin M3.

§4.4: a connected gap hides the faces across it only where the part beyond holds the probe. The probe is one point, so a face flush on a part thinner than δ shows on the higher-ranked part. Example: a Wedge bevel shows a band δ/b of the contact where the Block ranks higher, and nothing where the Wedge does (MIN_DIM). Also C09's 5.9 %, the diagonal cut's quarter, and F5 0.0989 → 0.1563.
§4.9: T-PERF-01 runs in the whole suite's one process, in path order, after 600 of its 736 cases; 'after every other spec' is gone.

§5's promise: O10's gloss is corrected ('hidden' is buried, on a higher-ranked part's face, or with the probe inside another part) and the thin partner is added with V1's figures. The O11 bullet gains a Wedge's surface samples (C09's bevel 0.0007) and a round part's sampled overlap under a shift (G 0.0001).
§5.2: M2's surface samples of a round part or a Wedge follow its writing (C09's bevel ΔG 0.0007, O11); the paragraph is re-wrapped.

§5.6: the writing row gains every fixture's Wedges written their other way (only C09's bevel, −0.0022 on the Blade, ΔG 0.0007). The 2 % rule row gains the thin partner: its gloss, the diagonal-cut figures, and bevel bands of 5.9 % on C09 and at most 0.33 % elsewhere.
§14.1 L1 row: --quick takes 30.2–30.7 s under ordinary load, so the gate needs a quiet machine.

§14.11 T-PERF-01: what was measured under ordinary load (V2, fixer D, and my verify's F2 stretch of 0.489 ms); the quiet figures need a quiet machine; verify runs it in path order as the 601st of 736 cases.

§16.18 numeric guards row: SAMPLE_X and SAMPLE_Y place the raster's samples and move values, as GOLDEN does. 0.0012 / 0.0018 moves 14 of the 70 golden entries (C06's EdgeLength, P2's chains, P5's cutIndex …) but no d, so a change goes with BALANCE_VERSION.

§17.1 O10: a new paragraph on the point probe and thin partners. It covers V1's figures, the Block/Wedge band, and the bands on the §5.5 fixtures (mostly Wedge thin edges, also a narrow Block's edge beside a curved face).

§17.1 O10, options: (i) as built: the band only adds exposed area in the measure, and can keep a part in the verdict. (ii) the segment probe: §5.5 figures, the diagonal cut closed, 5,191 d moves and 197 Hard → Normal tiers on the plausible set (185 built on C09), 24 rises from the sub-grid budget, cost × 1.04–1.27 (about 65 ms quiet). The verdict's half is described: each hider's half-spaces swept along the normal.
§17.1 O10, question and default: the question now offers (i) or (ii); the default is (i).

§17.1 O11: 'another writing takes the same probes and chords'. M2's surface samples of a Wedge follow its writing (C09's bevel 15, Sharpening 0.1904 → 0.1897). A Wedge's surface grid is added to the study and to the question.

§17.2: the checkpoint row's 'runs it last' is fixed and gains the ordinary-load figures. The 2 % rule row gets the corrected gloss and the thin partner with a segment probe's cost. The invisible-construction row gets a Wedge's surface samples.

E-S2.13 (docs/spec/SPEC-evidence.md): the introduction now names fixer E's work. The writings sentence gains the Wedges written their other way. The X mirror's cause is added (#24's Wedge tip, the walk's world sign, τ figures, 0.3697 dense).

deviations: E2's order: the SPEC used 'after every other spec' only to explain the larger heap behind the stretches it reports past 0.35. Its asserted figures are taken with T-PERF-01 run alone, and the heap reason holds at its place in path order. openIssues: Decision for the lead (**[Decision to confirm]**, §17.1 O10): the point probe as built (i) against a segment probe (ii). (i) lets an invisible diagonal cut reach Hard, and C09 carries 0.077 / 0.095 of band. (ii) closes that, plays 197 plausible designs a tier lower, and costs about × 1.19 on the slowest design (about 65 ms quiet, past the 60 ms guard). The verdict half of (ii) is unbuilt and unmeasured: it would move verdicts and E-S2.12's figures.
Not measured: whether a band keeps a part in the verdict that the truth would clean.

T-PERF-01 has not run on a quiet machine on this tree. Under the user's ordinary load it fails on a total (worst valid 8 at 61–62 ms, fixer D) or a stretch (F2 0.489 ms, this run). README now says verify is not green until a quiet run passes.
The segment variant's cost was timed under heavy load (26–82 %); a quiet re-time would firm up the × 1.19.
S-PAR-02's digest is unchanged this round, since no value moved; the Studio runs use fixer D's parity.bv1.digest.txt.
